title: SharePoint and OneDrive: updated search experience with Copilot Search
summary: The rollout windows, administrator deadline and Restricted Content Discovery controls are supported. The briefing correctly distinguishes existing Copilot app licensing from unpublished terms for the new search surfaces. Its statement that most people find files through search is unconfirmed and should be narrowed.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery prerequisites include an organisational Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Ensure your organization has a Microsoft Copilot license. Restricted Content Discovery is intended for Microsoft Copilot deployment and governance scenarios.

claims.claim: By default only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: The control is at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. ... Select the site you want to configure. ... Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for the site.

claims.claim: Learn documents no administrator UI path or automation command for deferring this updated search experience.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Search defer SharePoint tenant site settings; Copilot Search Set-SPOSite Set-SPOTenant search experience opt out. Read Search management and FAQ; returned KnowledgeAgent and Site AI controls concern separate Copilot in SharePoint, not search deferral.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is an existing site-level content-discovery control rather than a search-interface deferral switch.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting. When you turn on the setting, Microsoft 365 search systems propagate it so that content from the site doesn't appear in organization-wide discovery experiences.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery applies to SharePoint sites and is not supported for OneDrive sites.
claims.quote: You can only apply this feature to SharePoint sites. It's not supported for OneDrive sites.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not affect searches originating from site context.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't affect searches that originate from site context or other intelligent experiences such as Microsoft 365 Feed and Recommendations.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery affects organisation-wide search experiences such as SharePoint home and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery affects organization-wide search experiences (SharePoint home, Office.com, Bing) and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including experiences that rely on tenant-wide content discovery.

claims.claim: The Copilot Search management page describes an ownership or recent-interaction exception to Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: This setting prevents these sites from appearing in organization-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot answers unless a user owns or has recently interacted with content on those sites.

claims.claim: The Restricted Content Discovery page describes limiting discovery including recently interacted files, differing from the management page's exception.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery helps you limit discovery of content from specific SharePoint sites, including recently interacted files, in organization-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot responses while those reviews are taking place.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Microsoft describes Restricted Content Discovery as a temporary governance control for permissions reviews.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is designed as a temporary governance control that gives organizations time to review and right-size access while continuing their Copilot deployment.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery changes need propagation time, which can be long for large sites.
claims.quote: For sites with more than 500,000 items, an update to Restricted Content Discovery could take more than a week to fully process and reflect in search and Copilot experiences.
